question: How do we protect our 6.2472 held shares while enforcing a strict 1.50:1 hurdle on new capital?

epigraph.quote: Hold existing Stage 2 exposure behind a ratcheted hard stop, but refuse to commit fresh dollars when normalized reward-to-risk falls short.
epigraph.author: Portfolio Capital-Allocation Discipline

web_blocks.title: 9.1 Steelmanning Both Sides: Bull Thesis vs. Bear Thesis

web_blocks.html: The Bull Steelman: Cheniere runs 56 mtpa of premier U.S. Gulf Coast liquefaction backed by $112.2 billion of revenue backlog (~15-year average SPA life) [2][31]. CCL Stage 3 finished ahead of schedule in August 2026, Midscale 8&9 is 58.6% built for 2H 2028 startup, and SPL Expansion Phase 1 holds a FERC Final EIS with ~50% term-loan commitments [3][31]. Its -0.40 effective beta also shields a tech-heavy portfolio during an S&P 500 Downtrend [42].

The Bear Steelman: After a +51.67% YTD rally, $294.84 prices in peak 2026 margins inflated by Strait of Hormuz spikes ($28.51/MMBtu TTF; 352 TBtu of 9M short-term marketing) [31][35][39]. Gross debt climbed to $24.138 billion with a -$523 million working-capital deficit, 60.2% of net debt inside 48.6%-owned CQP, and $1.2 billion of 5.800% 2037 notes closed November 17 [31][32]. With U.S. exports projected to hit 19.0 Bcf/d in 2027, normalized net FCF yields only 5.31% versus a 5.04% 10-year Treasury [35][36][42].
The scenario and horizon tables below weigh Cheniere's 12-month expected return against the 5.04% Treasury benchmark and map the decision rules for each timeframe.

web_blocks.takeaway: The probability-weighted 12-month expected price equals $304.00 (+3.11% vs. $294.84 CMP, plus ~0.79% dividend yield), lagging the 5.04% 10-year Treasury rate. Retaining 100% of our 6.2472 Schwab shares is justified strictly as a -0.40-beta Stage 2 hedge above $281.56, with zero hesitation on trimming at $315–$325 or exiting below $281.56.

web_blocks.takeaway: Separating existing shares from new capital prevents FOMO while protecting current upside. New capital is REJECTED (TIER_0) because even the $287.06–$295.80 support zone yields only 1.35:1 asymmetry to $315.00.

web_blocks.html: Active Holding Action: We hold 6.2472 shares in Charles Schwab (cost $1,999.95 or $320.14/share; value $1,841.92; unrealized loss -$158.03; 2.45% weight) [42]. LNG holds a confirmed Stage 2 trend above our prior $278.52 stop and carries a portfolio-stabilizing -0.40 beta. We assign HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP (0 shares sold now) and ratchet the hard stop up to $281.56 (50D SMA $286.33 minus 0.5x ATR14) [42].

web_blocks.intro: Our execution grid separates our new-capital REJECTED verdict (0.0% allocation, TIER_0) from our Schwab holding plan. We trail the hard stop up to $281.56 (+$3.04 above prior $278.52).

web_blocks.html: If $281.56 triggers—or for any incremental dollar evaluated today—our 100% redeployment plan prioritizes defense inside a market Downtrend [42]. Portfolio cash sits at just $2,540.35 (3.38% of $75,110.60 net worth) against our 22.0% Downtrend floor. We therefore direct 70.0% to Cash / T-Bills, 30.0% to Stage 2 shortlist ETF XLV ($177.24 inside $173.85–$179.15, $163.04 stop, $206.00 target for 1.67:1 R:R), and 0.0% to Stage 3 peer Shell (SHEL) [41][42].

Action & Re-Rating Triggers: Exit all 6.2472 Schwab shares on a daily close below $281.56; trim into strength between $315.00 and $325.00 without a new SPA/FID catalyst. Upgrade new capital from REJECTED only if contracted 2028+ EBITDA reaches ≥$8.0B, or if price resets into a fresh Stage 1/2 base near $224.00–$231.00 (restoring ≥7.0% normalized net FCF yield on 204.2M current / 198.0M forward shares; $258.00 yields just 6.07%–6.26%) with a new-base structural stop below that lower band (≤$206.00 at $224.00 or ≤$220.00 at $258.00) so R:R to $315.00 clears ≥1.50:1 rather than referencing the current $281.56 held stop.

book_paragraphs: We have reached our synthesis chapter, where business forensics, valuation, and live price action meet the portfolio ledger. Let us begin by giving both sides of the Cheniere debate their strongest honest hearing.

On the bull side, Cheniere controls 56 million tonnes per year of operational U.S. liquefaction capacity backed by $112.2 billion in contracted backlog. Corpus Christi Stage 3 finished ahead of schedule in August 2026, Midscale Trains 8 and 9 stand 58.6% complete for 2028 startup, and Sabine Pass Expansion Phase 1 holds a Final Environmental Impact Statement and half its term-loan commitments. Inside our tech-heavy portfolio, Cheniere's -0.40 beta also buffers market downturns.

On the bear side, two Pass 1 blind spots alter the valuation math. First, 2026 cash flow benefited from Strait of Hormuz disruptions that lifted TTF and JKM above $28 per MMBtu and sent nine-month short-term marketing volumes up 73% to 352 TBtu. As Venture Global and Golden Pass lift U.S. exports toward 19.0 Bcf/d in 2027, normalized EBITDA settles near $7.30 billion rather than $9.00 billion. Second, gross debt expanded to $24.14 billion at Q3 2026—with a $523 million working-capital deficit and $1.2 billion of 5.800% 2037 parent notes—leaving a 5.31% normalized net free cash flow yield against a 5.04% 10-year Treasury.

Weighting our three 12-month scenarios—25% Bear at $195.00, 55% Base at $315.00, and 20% Bull at $410.00—yields an expected price of $304.00. That +3.11% expected return sits below the risk-free Treasury yield. Even from the $295.80 support top, upside to $315.00 ($19.20) versus our ratcheted $281.56 stop ($14.24) equals 1.35-to-1, failing our 1.50-to-1 hurdle.

Our dual verdict is clear. For new capital, we assign REJECTED (TIER_0) on valuation and cash-flow normalization, refusing to hedge behind wait-for-support when support itself fails 1.50-to-1 math. For our existing 6.2472 Schwab shares ($1,841.92, 2.45% weight), we assign HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP and ratchet our stop upward from $278.52 to $281.56 just under Pivot S1 and the rising 50-day average. If $281.56 breaks, we exit all 6.2472 shares and allocate 70% to Treasury cash and 30% to Stage 2 healthcare ETF XLV.

book_subsections.title: Why Separating New Capital from Held Shares Matters Here
paragraphs: Beginners often expect one label for both fresh cash and an existing holding. In reality, portfolio correlation and trend momentum create an asymmetry. Holding 2.45% of the portfolio in a Stage 2 negative-beta hedge with just 4.5% downside to $281.56 risks only 11 basis points of portfolio value.

Adding fresh dollars at 1.35-to-1 normalized asymmetry in a Downtrend market is a poor bet, so our risk budget rejects it. If Cheniere rallies into $315 to $325 on Hormuz headlines without new contracted capacity, we harvest into strength.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Good underwriting does not bend numbers to match last week's target. Re-testing Cheniere without prior-verdict bias revealed that Hormuz windfalls and $24.14 billion of expanding debt compress normalized reward-to-risk below 1.50:1—turning new capital to REJECTED while trailing our held stop upward to $281.56.
